items.title: Snow Brings Austria to a Standstill
items.gist: A heavy November snowfall disrupted roads, trains and flights across Austria. The snow may stay for days, while colder weather brings new risks.
items.summary: Snow fell across much of Austria on Thursday. The A21 motorway near Vienna was closed in both directions for several hours after vehicles got stuck. Emergency services dealt with hundreds of calls, and flights at Vienna Airport were delayed by de-icing. Several other roads and rail lines were also affected. Forecasters said the snow could remain as temperatures drop.
items.host_open: Austria woke up to a very white commute. How did the snow affect your day?

items.title: Experts Criticise Prosecutor Plan
items.gist: Legal experts say Austria’s proposed federal prosecution office needs a fresh start. They warn the current draft could leave prosecutors exposed to political pressure.
items.summary: Legal experts criticised the government’s latest plan for a federal prosecution office. They say it does not provide enough independence from political influence. One concern is that parliament could have an ongoing role in overseeing the office, including during investigations. The government needs a two-thirds majority in parliament to pass the measure. The Greens say they will not negotiate until a substantially revised draft is presented.
items.host_open: A watchdog needs room to do its job. Does this debate surprise you?

items.title: Vienna Plans Major Culture Cuts
items.gist: Vienna says it must save €31 million from its culture budget. The cuts could affect theatres, festivals and popular summer events.
items.summary: Vienna’s culture department must save €31 million in its 2027 budget. The city says the cuts are part of efforts to reduce its debt. Subsidies for several theatres and festivals will fall, and the Kultursommer will be stopped. The Klima Biennale will also be paused. Some arts organisations say the scale and short notice of the cuts make it hard to respond.
items.host_open: Vienna’s cultural calendar may get a little quieter. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: Russia Warns Ukraine’s Power Grid
items.gist: Ukraine says Russia may launch another major strike on energy infrastructure. The warning comes as the country asks partners for more air-defence supplies.
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia was preparing a major attack on energy sites and other critical services. Russian strikes have already damaged Ukraine’s power network during the war. Ukraine is asking partners for more air-defence equipment, including interceptors for Patriot systems. US envoy Jared Kushner said talks with Russia had reached a deadlock over Ukrainian territory. Ukrainian and European leaders say Russia has not shown a willingness to compromise.
items.host_open: A winter power supply is vital for millions of people. How worried are you by this warning?

items.title: Deadly Strikes Reported in Gaza
items.gist: Hospital officials say Israeli strikes killed ten people in Gaza. Israel says one strike targeted a Hamas official and other militants.
items.summary: Hospital officials in Gaza said ten people were killed in several strikes and a shooting overnight and on Thursday. They said the dead included a man and his wife in an apartment in Deir al-Balah. Israeli leaders said the military killed a Hamas official responsible for economic and education affairs. Israel’s military said one strike targeted three militants. Officials did not immediately comment on all the reported strikes and deaths. The attacks happened despite a ceasefire deal reached more than a year ago.
items.host_open: Families are grieving after another deadly night in Gaza. How do you feel about the latest reports?

items.title: Iranian Drones Kill Italians in Kuwait
items.gist: Two Italian civilian workers were killed in a drone attack in Kuwait, according to Italy’s foreign ministry. Iran denied responsibility, and the incident adds to regional tensions.
items.summary: Two Italian civilians were killed and two others injured in a drone attack in Kuwait. Italy said the workers were technicians maintaining radar systems for a defence contractor. Kuwait said its air defences had shot down several drones from Iran. Iran’s foreign minister offered condolences but denied that Iran was behind the attack. The incident comes amid wider conflict and repeated attacks in the Gulf region.
items.host_open: Two workers lost their lives far from home. How does this news make you feel?

items.title: EU Leaders Clash Over Ukraine Loan
items.gist: EU leaders are divided over a proposed €45 billion loan for Ukraine. Some governments want all member states to take part; others want to opt out.
items.summary: EU leaders met in Brussels to discuss the bloc’s next long-term budget and support for Ukraine. The proposal includes a €45 billion loan for Ukraine in 2027. Germany argues that all EU members should back it. Slovakia, Hungary and Czechia want to opt out of the loan. Leaders are also divided over the size of the wider EU budget and how its money should be spent.
items.host_open: The EU budget meeting has a very large price tag. Did you expect this much disagreement?

items.title: Spain Faces a Tight Election
items.gist: Spain votes on Sunday in an early parliamentary election. Polls and campaign coverage suggest a possible shift towards a conservative coalition that could include the far right.
items.summary: Spain is due to hold an early general election on Sunday, November 29. The campaign has focused in part on immigration and the role of the far-right Vox party. Vox says it wants policies to give Spanish citizens priority over foreign residents and immigrants. The party could seek to govern with the conservative People’s Party if the election results allow it. The outcome could change Spain’s government and its approach to migration.
items.host_open: Spain’s ballot could reshape its government. Did that possibility surprise you?

items.title: Late Night Turns to Turkey Pardon
items.gist: The White House’s annual turkey-pardon tradition became a late-night topic this week. Jimmy Kimmel and Seth Meyers covered the event in recent monologues.
items.summary: The White House held its annual ceremony to pardon Thanksgiving turkeys. The event is a long-running seasonal tradition in US politics. Jimmy Kimmel discussed the ceremony in a monologue on November 24. Seth Meyers also joked about a question President Donald Trump asked while discussing the turkey. The ceremony itself is symbolic and does not change government policy.
items.host_open: The White House has a turkey tradition unlike any other. Did that surprise you?

items.title: A Spanish Economist Tipped for ECB
items.gist: EU diplomats say Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos is set to lead the European Central Bank. He is expected to succeed Christine Lagarde next year.
items.summary: EU leaders and diplomats backed Spanish economist Pablo Hernández de Cos for the next ECB presidency. He is expected to succeed Christine Lagarde, who is due to leave the post early in February. The Netherlands had supported its own candidate, Klaas Knot, but signalled support for a consensus choice. The ECB sets interest rates for the euro area. The appointment still has to follow the formal EU process.
items.host_open: A new ECB chief could shape everyday borrowing costs. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: Britain Reaches Davis Cup Semis
items.gist: Great Britain beat Germany in a deciding doubles match to reach the Davis Cup semi-finals. It is the team’s first appearance at that stage since 2019.
items.summary: Great Britain defeated Germany in a deciding doubles match at the Davis Cup. Henry Patten and Neal Skupski won the key match for the British team. The result sent Britain into the semi-finals for the first time since 2019. Germany had been aiming to continue its run in the competition. The Davis Cup is an international team tennis tournament.
items.host_open: One doubles match decided the tie. Did you see that result coming?
